Uomo di 63 anni con carcinoma della pros: 63-year-old man with prostate carcinoma. Follow-up 68Ga-PSMA PET-CT, about 6 months after the prior PSMA PET-CT; treatment in the meantime not stated in the collection. The images and report of the prior exam are available.

La PET-TC con PSMA (antigene di membrana:
PSMA PET-CT (prostate-specific membrane antigen) shows prostate carcinoma and its metastases with much higher contrast than CT: lymph nodes of a few millimeters are already positive. In the first exam the disease was extensive: prostate, pelvic, retroperitoneal and mediastinal lymph nodes and a focus in the left ischium (non-regional lymph node and bone metastases, M1b).

At follow-up, comparison is made site by site: here most lesions no longer show uptake and the prostate is greatly reduced, but three small avid lymph nodes and the left ischial focus remain: partial response. A focus near the pelvic wall must be localized on CT with the bone window: here what looks like an obturator lymph node lies within the ischium. Dedicated criteria (for example RECIP 1.0, which uses total tumor volume and new lesions; or the PPP progression criteria) also consider the appearance of new lesions, which are absent here.

Beware of physiological PSMA uptake (salivary and lacrimal glands, kidneys, spleen, liver, bowel, bladder) and of false positives: sympathetic ganglia, fractures and benign bone lesions, some non-prostatic neoplasms.

PET-TC con 68Ga-PSMA (acquisizione circa:
68Ga-PSMA PET-CT (acquisition about 55 minutes after injection); low-dose CT for fusion. Weight 85 kg.

Intense uptake in the prostate, extending to both lobes. Avid lymph nodes: small left iliac, right iliac, right common iliac, retroperitoneal (left para-aortic and interaortocaval), a large lower posterior mediastinal lymph node (right paraesophageal/retrocrural, SUVmax about 70) and an upper paraesophageal lymph node. Avid focus in the left ischium (posterior column of the acetabulum, SUVmax about 24) without evident CT changes: bone metastasis. No visceral lesions.
Physiological uptake in salivary glands, kidneys, spleen, liver and bowel; urinary excretion.

Conclusions: prostate carcinoma with pelvic, retroperitoneal and mediastinal lymph node metastases and bone metastasis of the left ischium (M1b).

68Ga-PSMA PET-CT (acquisition about 55 minutes after injection); low-dose CT for fusion. Weight 85 kg.

Intense uptake of the prostate, extending to both lobes. Avid lymph nodes: small left iliac, right iliac, right common iliac, retroperitoneal (left para-aortic and interaortocaval), a large lower posterior mediastinal lymph node (paraesophageal/right retrocrural, SUVmax about 70), and an upper paraesophageal lymph node. Avid focus in the left ischium (posterior column of the acetabulum, SUVmax about 24) without evident changes on CT: bone metastasis. No visceral lesions.
Physiologic uptake of kidneys, spleen, liver, and bowel; urinary excretion (head and upper neck not assessable: obscured for anonymity).

Conclusions: prostate carcinoma with pelvic, retroperitoneal, and mediastinal lymph node metastases and a bone metastasis of the left ischium (M1b).
